root_idea.summary: The core lexical orientation is sweet, palatable water.
root_idea.development: The central usage describes water as sweet and thirst-relieving. Related Classical Arabic usage includes a verb meaning “to become sweet” and extensions of فُرَاتٌ as the Euphrates and, poetically, the sea.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is a Quran-attested adjective and is presented under the normalized citation form فُرَاتٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: An adjectival وصف of water, used with both singular and plural nouns; the sense emphasizes water that relieves thirst by its sweetness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become sweet, of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal usage; the infinitive فُرُوتَةٌ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act viciously or unrighteously, or to commit adultery or fornication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal usage equated with فَجَرَ; variant vocalizations and the infinitive فَرْتٌ are reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak in intellect after having possessed ample intelligence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported verbal usage with a change in intellectual capacity as its result.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A span: the space measured by extending the thumb and forefinger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A variant of فِتْر, reportedly formed by transposition; it denotes the corresponding measure.
As a geographical name; الفُرَاتَانِ denotes the Euphrates together with the Tigris or, in another reported usage, the Dujayl.
A rare poetic appellation, attested in a verse describing pearls.
A feminine lexical usage; the word’s derivational relation to فَرَتَ is reported with disagreement over whether ن is radical.
A separately reported lexical usage of the same form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The son of a female slave who is a fornicatress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional kinship expression built with الفَرْتَنَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low, ignoble, mean, or sordid person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression with the form ابنُ فَرْتَنَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a certain woman.
The young one of a hyena.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The verb meaning “to be or become sweet” is represented under its own headword.
The viciousness and sexual-misconduct branch is represented.
The intellectual weakening branch is represented.
The span or measure meaning is represented.
The adjective meaning sweet water is represented as the Quranic sense.
The geographical name and paired-rivers construction are represented.
The poetic sea usage is represented.
All reported lexical branches and conventional expressions in the unit are represented.

cautions: The Quranic adjective فُرَاتٌ meaning sweet water should not be conflated with the separate Classical noun used as the geographical name of the Euphrates or with its rare poetic use for the sea.
The derivational analysis of فَرْتَنَا is reported as disputed, although its listed lexical usages are preserved.
